title: An unprojected SECOND dimension draws a grouped chart with no series and says nothing — `hasNoCategoryKey` has no counterpart on the series axis
body:
Measured while implementing #4673 (PR #4681), filed rather than widened into it.

## What is wrong

The "known to be empty versus cannot know" split is now answered on both of the pivot's dimensions for the BUCKETING half (#4673): a row whose second-dimension value is `null`/`''` gets a drawn series, and a row that does not carry the group key at all gets no bucket and contributes no column.

The ANNOUNCING half only exists for the first dimension. `AdvancedChartImpl`'s `hasNoCategoryKey` (framework#4033) names an unprojected x-axis dimension instead of drawing an empty axis. There is no counterpart for the series dimension, so a pivot whose second dimension was never projected renders as:

- axes, grid, tooltip and legend frame drawn;
- zero series, therefore zero marks;
- no explanation anywhere.

Concretely: `dimensions: ['status', 'priority']`, `values: ['est_hours']`, where the result rows carry `status` and `est_hours` but no `priority` key at all. `buildChartSeries` returns `series: []` and one bucket row per status.

## Why this is worth a card rather than a shrug

It is the same sentence #4466 was filed over — a chart that is not merely empty but says nothing about why — and the platform has already ruled twice that "cannot know" must REFUSE LOUDLY rather than draw nothing (framework#4033, and the delegated ruling on #4673, 2026-08-15). An empty grouped chart currently reads to the author as "no data matched", when what happened is that a dimension they grouped by never arrived.

Note this behaviour is not NEW in #4673: before it, the unprojected group's measure was written under the `''` key, which was also bound to no series, so the mark count was the same. What changed is only that the phantom column is no longer written.

## Not the same card as #4507

#4507 is that the pivot writes `[xKey]` onto every bucket it creates, so `hasNoCategoryKey` can never fire for the FIRST dimension of a pivoted chart — a guard that exists but is blinded. This is the SECOND dimension, where no guard exists to blind. Fixing #4507 does not produce this one's answer.

Related: #4507, #4673, #4681, #4466, framework#4033.
